## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater euglenoid characterized by narrow elliptical to spindle-shaped green cells with a rigid pellicle, fine longitudinal or slightly spiral striations, and a short pointed projection at the rear of the cell. Lepocinclis steinii contains numerous small, disc-shaped chloroplasts and typically two large ring-shaped paramylon bodies used for carbohydrate storage. It occurs as part of the plankton in freshwater ponds, lakes, reservoirs, ditches, and other standing or slow-moving waters, including vegetated and nutrient-rich habitats. Like other photosynthetic euglenoids, it contributes to primary production and forms part of the microbial food web in freshwater ecosystems.
